what: The Anthropic chain in one environment: Anthropic's eth/ proof ported to complexitylib's Lean (v4.36.0-rc2) proves MainResults.ethIsFalse against the vendored MainResults.lean, and with C2 gives ¬ETH on cslib's multitape Turing machine, decided here with our statement pin, axioms files, nanoda (two negative controls), leanchecker --fresh, three planted variants, and Lean's own judge (lake comparator --paranoid, six checkers).

claim.authors: the statement by hand; the port and the corollary by an AI agent (Claude), in claimbox

scope: ETH (complexitylib's, on cslib's deterministic multitape Turing machine with encCNF) is false, from Anthropic's own proof through C2, every step elaborated and checked in one Lean (v4.36.0-rc2): no step from Anthropic's proof to the standard machine crosses a version seam. Decided: the statement byte-equal to the pin, MainResults.lean byte-equal to Anthropic's, the three standard axioms, nanoda accepting all 77,276 declarations beneath it, leanchecker --fresh, the three planted variants refused, and lake comparator --paranoid accepting with all six checkers (con-leche and con-ron: 74,801 declarations).
reading: The proof that checks here is a modified copy of Anthropic's: 47 of its 809 files were changed to build on the newer Lean and Mathlib (renames, imports, tactic repairs; 45 declarations changed text only by a forced rename; every change listed with both sha256s in PORT.md). Lean checks whatever proof is there against Anthropic's unchanged statement, so the port changes nothing that is decided; it is said here because the proof is not Anthropic's bytes.
This closes the second version seam for Anthropic's chain only. OpenAI's statement reaches ETHIsFalse inside OpenAI's Lean (v4.34.1, Hawkley's chain); that seam is read, not decided.
Lean's judge ran without its sandbox (bubblewrap cannot create a user namespace on RunPod's containers). The sandbox protects the judge from a hostile build; the build here is our own claimbox's.
claimbox and cert-machine have the same operator: this decision separates the roles of author and checker; it is not a second party.
